$comment: MCP servers for TAAS. Committed deliberately: every operator needs the same
registration. No secret appears here, and no per-operator path either -
tt-atlassian-mcp and tt-bitbucket-mcp are vendored inside this repo under
src/, so ${workspaceFolder} resolves the same way for everyone who clones it.
Neither authenticates through TAAS: tt-bitbucket-mcp never contacts Bitbucket
at all, and tt-atlassian-mcp reads its own .env file next to its script -
see src/tt-atlassian-mcp/README.md to set that up once.
Local toolchain. stdio only; no network listener is opened.
No --env-file flag here deliberately: `uv run --env-file .env` fails hard
if .env does not exist yet, and .env is gitignored - a fresh clone has none
until someone runs `cp .env.example .env`. Nothing is required by default
(see config.py's REQUIRED), so this starts with zero setup. If you create a
`.env` to override a default, add --env-file .env to your own local copy of
this file, or export the variables in your shell before opening VS Code -
config.load() reads only the process environment; it never parses .env
itself.
READ-ONLY. Jira and Confluence. The source protocols declare no write
method. This is the agent's own interactive session; the toolchain spawns
a second, separate instance of the same script for bulk ingestion (U2-01).
READ-ONLY. Repositories, endpoints, commit history - read from git clones
already on disk. Never contacts Bitbucket's network API.

playwright.$comment: Live exploration of the application under test. Read-only against the AUT.
